feasibility_classes.easy_feasible: Slack SLA. Many historical matches. Live seed should succeed from warm-start, usually on the first attempt.
feasibility_classes.tight_feasible: Historically jointly feasible with a modest match count. Live seed still has matching runs.
feasibility_classes.edge_feasible: At or just inside a bound. Very few historical and/or live matches. Stresses ranking quality, not HITL.
feasibility_classes.historical_optimistic: Warm-start history is jointly feasible for the chosen algorithm, but live seed 210 has zero matching runs on that algorithm. Tests retrieval optimism vs the new instance.
feasibility_classes.minor_relaxation: Requested SLA is slightly beyond a bound. HITL offers each algorithm's best-known value x 1.05 (x 0.95 for security). Picking an offer also selects that algorithm for live search.
feasibility_classes.jointly_infeasible: Each hard constraint is independently attainable but no stored run meets them together. HITL offers per-algorithm conditional relaxations.
feasibility_classes.independently_infeasible: At least one threshold is beyond the independent best-known value. HITL offers each algorithm's best-known x 1.05 (x 0.95 for security).
feasibility_classes.relaxation_insufficient_for_live: History is infeasible. Both algorithm-tagged 5% HITL offers restore a historical region, but live seed 210 still cannot meet either offered threshold.
feasibility_classes.deeply_infeasible: Far outside the attainable region. Independent 5% offers may still leave a joint hole.
feasibility_classes.unconstrained: No numeric hard SLA. Proposer ranks purely by primary_objective.
feasibility_classes.parser_unresolved: Expected parse_failed=true. Operator must rewrite before search.
feasibility_classes.auto_switched: best_fit is not jointly feasible, app_rollout is. Feasibility proceeds without HITL and selects app_rollout for live search.

categories: historical_optimistic vs easy_feasible (same linguistic style, different live outcome)
auto_switched vs independently_infeasible on nearby latency SLAs
non_relaxable vs relaxable on the same SLA
hitl per-algorithm offers (best_fit fast vs app_rollout tighter/slower)

expected_field_rules.relaxation_order: Only metrics the operator text explicitly allows loosening (relax / loosen / if needed / if stuck / you may). A hard constraint alone is not enough. The metric must also appear in hard_constraints. In-loop Recalibrator will not loosen a metric missing from this list.
expected_field_rules.non_relaxable_constraints: Only never / always / in all cases, or an explicit non-relaxable statement. 'must stay under' is a hard SLA, not a non-relaxable flag. HITL hides Relax when the metric is in this list.
expected_field_rules.hitl_vs_in_loop: HITL Relax is gated by non_relaxable_constraints. In-loop Recalibrator is gated by relaxation_order AND not non_relaxable.

intents.text: Optimize for low latency. Average latency must stay under 1000ms. Cost and security are secondary.
intents.thesis_insight: Baseline first-try success. Warm-start should return matching runs and the verifier should pass without HITL or in-loop relaxation.
intents.parser_note: 'must stay under' is a hard SLA, not a never-relax keyword. Same sentence as the UI latency preset. Contrast POL-01 which uses 'never'.

intents.text: Keep mean per-app latency at or below 700 milliseconds. Prefer the lowest latency you can still achieve under that cap.
intents.thesis_insight: Comfortable but no longer slack. Distinguishes whether warm-start ranking still finds a good latency corner when the filter is narrower than LAT-01.
intents.parser_note: No relax/loosen cue, so relaxation_order is empty even though latency is a hard constraint.

intents.text: Average latency must stay under 550ms. Security and cost are soft preferences only.
intents.thesis_insight: Above the 508 ms best_fit floor, so Feasibility stays on best_fit. Live best_fit can do about 520 ms. Contrast with LAT-05 (500 ms), which auto-switches to app_rollout, and with POL-01 (470 ms), which pauses.

intents.text: We need average latency no worse than 521 ms. Optimize latency, cost and security are not main concerns.
intents.thesis_insight: 521 ms is just above live best_fit (520.266 ms). History is jointly feasible on best_fit (floor 508.131 ms). Tests ranking quality at the live edge without pausing.

intents.text: Optimize for low latency. Average latency must stay under 500ms. Cost and security are secondary.
intents.thesis_insight: 500 ms is below the best_fit floor (508.131 ms) but above the app_rollout floor (484.896 ms). Feasibility auto-switches to app_rollout and does not pause. Live rollout can do 491.834 ms (2 matching rows) and live best_fit cannot.

intents.text: Interactive traffic only: average latency has to remain under 400 ms. Do what you can with cost and security after that.
intents.thesis_insight: Same independent HITL offers as LAT-08 (best_fit 533.537 ms, app_rollout 509.141 ms) but the relative concession is larger versus 400 ms. Picking the app_rollout offer also switches live search. Both offers are above live floors (520.266 / 491.834 ms).

intents.text: Hard real-time: average latency must stay under 200 milliseconds. Latency is the only thing that matters.
intents.thesis_insight: Physically unattainable on this topology. HITL still only offers the two algorithm-tagged bounds (533.537 ms on best_fit, 509.141 ms on app_rollout). The agent cannot invent a 200 ms placement, it can only surface those floors.

intents.text: Optimize for low latency. Average latency must stay under 470ms. Cost and security are secondary.
intents.thesis_insight: Canonical HITL two-offer demo (intents.md case 6). 470 ms is below both historical floors, so the operator sees best_fit at 533.537 ms (fast, live floor 520.266) and app_rollout at 509.141 ms (slower, live floor 491.834). Picking an offer also selects that algorithm. Contrast LAT-05 (500 ms auto-switches, no pause) and POL-01 (same 470 ms, Relax hidden).

intents.text: Minimize average cost. Keep cost at or below 1000. Latency and security are secondary.
intents.thesis_insight: Cost analogue of LAT-01. Warm-start should rank by lowest avg_cost among a large feasible slice.

intents.text: The budget cap is 700 cost units per app on average. Prefer cheaper placements whenever the cap is met.
intents.thesis_insight: Mid-range cost SLA. Still jointly feasible, but the cheap corner of the front is more constrained than COST-01.

intents.text: Average cost must not exceed 400. Optimize for cost. Latency and security can wait.
intents.thesis_insight: Well above the 305 historical floor (rollout) / 307 (best_fit) and the 329 live best_fit floor, but already on the cheap tail.

intents.text: Squeeze average cost down to 329 or less. Cost is the objective, the other two metrics are unconstrained.
intents.thesis_insight: Live best cost is 328.89, so 329 is the last integer threshold that live best_fit can still meet. One matching live row: a precision test of warm-start vs search.

intents.text: Stay under an average cost of 300. If the cap cannot be met you may loosen cost slightly.
intents.thesis_insight: Historical best is 306.536 (best_fit) / 305.052 (app_rollout), so HITL offers 321.863 and 320.304. Live best is 328.892 / 327.566, so neither offer succeeds. Contrast with SEC-05, where both offers clear live, and with LAT-08, where both latency offers clear live.

intents.text: We cannot spend more than 200 cost units per app on average. Make cost the primary objective.
intents.thesis_insight: Far below every observed cost. HITL offers 321.863 (best_fit) and 320.304 (app_rollout), both still below live 328.892 / 327.566, so continue-anyway and relax-to-offer both fail unless the operator rewrites the intent.

intents.text: Keep average cost at or below 306. Minimize cost. Latency and security are secondary.
intents.thesis_insight: Cost analogue of LAT-05, but the floor gap is tiny (best_fit 306.536 vs app_rollout 305.052). Feasibility auto-switches to app_rollout with only 2 historical matches. Live cost floors are 328.892 / 327.566, so search still fails. Shows that auto-switch is a historical decision, not a live guarantee. Contrast LAT-05, where the switched algorithm succeeds live.

intents.text: Keep average security at least 8. Prefer low latency. Cost can be sacrificed first if needed.
intents.thesis_insight: Checks that the parser emits security >= (not <=) and that warm-start sorts by highest neighborhood-averaged security.
intents.parser_note: 'Cost can be sacrificed' is a soft preference. Cost is not a hard constraint, so it cannot appear in relaxation_order.

intents.text: Average security score must be at least 12. Maximize security under that floor.
intents.thesis_insight: Still lots of matches, but the cheap/fast low-security corner is filtered out. Useful as the mid point on the security axis.

intents.text: Average security must stay at 14 or above. Security is the objective, keep latency and cost reasonable if possible.
intents.thesis_insight: High-security slice that live can still hit (max 14.86). Pairs with LS-04, where the same 14 combined with tight latency becomes a Pareto hole.

intents.text: Push average security to at least 14.86. Maximize security.
intents.thesis_insight: Equals the live best_fit maximum (14.86). Two live rows, any proposer micro-step away from those weights can miss the SLA.

intents.text: Average security must be at least 16. If that floor is impossible you may lower the security constraint a little.
intents.thesis_insight: Historical max is 15.2 (best_fit) / 15.38 (app_rollout), so HITL offers 14.44 and 14.611. Live max 14.86 / 14.94 clears both. Higher-is-better analogue of LAT-08.

intents.text: We require an average security score of at least 20. Security is the only priority.
intents.thesis_insight: Same HITL offers as SEC-05 (14.44 on best_fit, 14.611 on app_rollout) against a much more aggressive request. Tests whether the operator treats bound-based offers as honest rather than as almost 20.

intents.text: Average security must be at least 15.3. Maximize security. Latency and cost are secondary.
intents.thesis_insight: Security auto-switch: 15.3 sits between best_fit max 15.2 and app_rollout max 15.38, so Feasibility proceeds on app_rollout without HITL. Live max is only 14.86 / 14.94, so the verifier should fail. Pair with LAT-05 (auto-switch that works live) and GAP-03 (no auto-switch, same live miss).

intents.text: Average latency under 1000 ms and average cost under 1000. Prefer low latency. Security is a soft preference.
intents.thesis_insight: Easy two-metric box. Historical matches drop from 940 (latency-only) to 347 once cost <= 1000 is co-constrained, even though each bound is slack on its own.

intents.text: Keep average latency at most 800 ms and average cost at most 700. Optimize latency, security can be ignored.
intents.thesis_insight: Both bounds are independently easy, together only 42 historical rows and 2 live best_fit rows remain. A feasible pair that already feels scarce.

intents.text: Target average latency <= 650 ms and average cost <= 700. Latency is primary. If needed, relax cost first, then latency.
intents.thesis_insight: One live best_fit row. Explicit relaxation_order is present even though HITL should not fire: useful if search later fails and Recalibrator needs a tie-break.

intents.text: Average latency must stay under 700ms and average cost must stay under 400. Prefer low latency. If needed, relax cost first, then latency.
intents.thesis_insight: Pareto hole: 700 ms and cost 400 each exist, never together. HITL offers per-algorithm conditional relaxations: latency 962.389 (best_fit) / 931.313 (app_rollout) given cost 400, or cost 631.085 / 581.111 given latency 700.

intents.text: We want average latency under 800 ms while keeping average cost under 400. Prefer low cost if both cannot hold, you may relax latency second.
intents.thesis_insight: 800 ms and cost 400 each exist, never together (the old 800/600 pair is now jointly feasible on app_rollout). Primary is cost rather than latency, so after a HITL relax the proposer ranking should flip.
intents.parser_note: 'relax latency second' implies cost is first, both are hard constraints so both are listed.

intents.text: Average latency below 1000 ms and average security at least 8. Optimize latency. Cost is a soft preference.
intents.thesis_insight: Easy latency+security box. Opposite trade-off from LC-01: adding security >= 8 to latency <= 1000 only cuts 940 to 705, so the low-latency tail is mostly already secure enough.

intents.text: Hold average latency to 800 ms or less and average security to 14 or more. Prefer high security.
intents.thesis_insight: High security with a still-reasonable latency cap is jointly feasible (best latency given security 14 is approx. 565 ms). Contrast with LS-04 at 550 ms.

intents.text: Time-sensitive and reasonably isolated: average latency under 550 ms, average security at least 8. Latency is primary.
intents.thesis_insight: 550 ms is tight, security 8 is not. Jointly feasible on live (2 rows). The next step up in security (LS-04) falls off the front.

intents.text: Average latency must stay under 550 ms and average security must stay at least 14. Prefer low latency. If needed, relax security first.
intents.thesis_insight: Each bound is independently easy-ish, together they never co-occur. Per-algorithm HITL offers: latency 632.670 (best_fit) / 593.514 (app_rollout) given security 14, or security 12.046 / 12.635 given latency 550.
intents.parser_note: Text says 'relax security first' and never names latency as relaxable, so only security is listed.

intents.text: Keep average latency under 700 ms with average security at least 12. Optimize security, cost is secondary.
intents.thesis_insight: Interior of the latency-security front: feasible with a healthy live match count. Good control for LS-04.

intents.text: Average cost at most 800 and average security at least 14. Maximize security. Latency is a soft preference.
intents.thesis_insight: High security is compatible with a moderate cost cap (best security given cost 500 is 12.9, but 800 still reaches 15.38). Shows the cost-security elbow.

intents.text: Budget 450 cost units per app on average, and keep average security at least 8. Prefer low cost.
intents.thesis_insight: Cheap + modest security still co-exist. Contrast with CS-03, where security 10 at cost 380 is a hole of a few units.

intents.text: Average cost must stay under 380 and average security must be at least 10. Prefer low cost. If needed, relax security first, then cost.
intents.thesis_insight: Smallest Pareto gap in the catalog after tightening past the new rollout front. Per-algorithm HITL offers: cost 430.967 (best_fit) / 410.598 (app_rollout) given security 10, or security 9.158 / 9.082 given cost 380.

intents.text: Keep average cost under 450 and average security at least 12. Security is primary. Relax cost first if the pair is impossible.
intents.thesis_insight: Cost <= 450 and security >= 12 restores a joint hole after cost<=500 and security>=12 became jointly feasible on app_rollout. Still independently feasible on each metric.

intents.text: Average cost no more than 400 and average security at least 8. Minimize cost.
intents.thesis_insight: Control for CS-03: drop security from 10 to 8 and a similar cost cap becomes jointly feasible. Isolates the Pareto edge.

intents.text: Average latency under 1200 ms, average cost under 1200, average security at least 6. Prefer balanced placements, with latency as the primary objective.
intents.thesis_insight: Slack three-metric box. Parser must extract three hard constraints with mixed operators. Search should still be a first-try success.

intents.text: Meet all three: latency <= 1000 ms, cost <= 1000, security >= 8. Optimize latency. If needed, relax cost, then security, then latency.
intents.thesis_insight: Same latency/cost box as LC-01 plus security >= 8. Matches fall from 347 to 141: the third constraint is binding once cost is already in the picture. Checks that the parser extracts three mixed-operator SLAs.

intents.text: Latency at most 900 ms, cost at most 800, security at least 8. Prefer low latency.
intents.thesis_insight: One live best_fit row. A feasible triple sitting on the interior elbow (the single historical point near cost 788 / sec 10.3 / lat 721 is the spirit of this box).

intents.text: Average latency under 1000 ms, average cost under 500, average security at least 8. Cost is the primary objective.
intents.thesis_insight: Cost-tight triple that live still meets once. Binding constraint is cost, latency 1000 is almost slack given cost 500 (cheapest secure-enough runs are slow).

intents.text: Latency <= 1000 ms, cost <= 600, security >= 12. Prefer high security. Relax cost first if the triple cannot be met.
intents.thesis_insight: Four historical rows, one live best_fit. Security-heavy triple with a cost cap that still just closes. Good candidate for showing requested-vs-delivered bars on all three axes.

intents.text: All three at once: latency under 550 ms, cost under 800, security at least 8. Prefer low latency. If needed, relax cost, then security, then latency.
intents.thesis_insight: Pairwise, latency 550 + cost 800 is feasible (81 rows) and latency 550 + security 8 is feasible (68), but the triple is empty. HITL must reason about a 3-way hole, not a single-metric bound.

intents.text: Require latency under 400 ms, cost under 200, and security at least 20. Optimize all three, if stuck, relax cost first, then security, then latency.
intents.thesis_insight: Every axis is independently beyond its bound. Independent 5% offers are per-algorithm (latency 533.537 / 509.141, cost 321.863 / 320.304, security 14.44 / 14.611) and still do not form a jointly feasible box, because cheap and fast never co-occur. Relaxing one metric at a time cannot recover a 3-way utopia.

intents.text: Average latency must stay under 520 ms. Optimize latency. Cost and security are secondary.
intents.thesis_insight: Feasibility proceeds on best_fit (neighbor floor 508.131 ms). Live best_fit is 520.266 ms, so the verifier should fail. Live app_rollout has matching rows (491.834 ms) but auto-switch does not fire because best_fit is historically jointly feasible. Recalibrator cannot salvage it: the text never put latency in relaxation_order.

intents.text: Hold average cost to 320 or less. Minimize cost.
intents.thesis_insight: History has 15 runs at cost <= 320 (best 305.052). Live best is 328.9. No HITL pause, and Recalibrator cannot loosen cost because the text never authorized relaxation_order. Likely max-iteration failure.

intents.text: Average security must be at least 15. Maximize security. Latency and cost are secondary.
intents.thesis_insight: 179 historical rows reach 15.0, live max is 14.86. The pre-check will not ask the operator, which is exactly the retrieval-mismatch story.

intents.text: Average latency under 550 ms and average security at least 12. Prefer low latency.
intents.thesis_insight: Pairwise analogue of GAP-01: 28 historical co-occurrences, zero on live best_fit. LS-03 (security 8 at the same latency) is live-feasible, this one is not.

intents.text: Latency at most 800 ms, cost at most 800, security at least 10. Optimize latency.
intents.thesis_insight: Three historical rows make the pre-check green. Live has no such compromise point. Strongest triple-metric retrieval-mismatch case.

intents.text: We are time-sensitive. Average latency must never exceed 470ms. Cost and security are secondary.
intents.thesis_insight: Same 470 ms SLA as the HITL demos, but 'never' should hide the Relax button. Continue-anyway cannot loosen the threshold, loop should die on max iterations. 500 ms now auto-switches (see LAT-05), so HITL policy demos moved below 484.9 ms.

intents.text: This involves self-driving vehicles so latency should never exceed 550ms. Security must never drop below 14. Keep cost as low as possible.
intents.thesis_insight: Same numeric pair as LS-04, both non-relaxable. No Relax option. Continue dies at max iterations. New intent is the only way out. Domain wrapping plus dual 'never'.

intents.text: Optimize for low latency. Average latency should stay under 470ms. If that is not possible you may relax.
intents.thesis_insight: Choose Continue at HITL. After three distinct failed weights Recalibrator may loosen 470 toward the empirical best. Needs max_iterations 7–8. Complements POL-01 (no Relax) and LAT-05 (500 ms auto-switch, no pause).

intents.text: Average latency must never exceed 470 ms. If a solution is infeasible you may relax the latency constraint.
intents.thesis_insight: Parser stress: 'never' vs 'you may relax' in one sentence. Code should keep latency non-relaxable if 'never' wins, which is the conservative safety reading. 470 ms still HITL, 500 ms would auto-switch.
intents.parser_note: Conflicting cues: 'never' -> non_relaxable, 'you may relax' -> relaxation_order. Recalibrator still blocks because non_relaxable wins.

intents.text: Average cost must never exceed 300. Latency and security are secondary.
intents.thesis_insight: COST-05 plus non-relaxable. HITL would offer 321.863 / 320.304, but Relax is hidden, and live cannot meet 300 anyway. Hard infeasibility with no legal escape except a new intent.

intents.text: Optimize for low latency. Keep cost reasonably low and security reasonably high.
intents.thesis_insight: No hard SLA, so Feasibility always proceeds. Proposer ranks the full history by latency. Mentions all three metrics but only latency is the objective: tests soft_preferences vs empty hard_constraints.

intents.text: Minimize cost. Average latency must stay under 1000ms. Security should stay reasonably high.
intents.thesis_insight: Primary objective is not the constrained metric. Warm-start filters on latency then ranks by cost. Checks that the agent does not treat 'minimize cost' as a hidden cost <= ? SLA.

intents.text: Maximize security. Cost does not matter at all and may be sacrificed. There is no numeric SLA.
intents.thesis_insight: Unconstrained higher-is-better ranking. Historical best security is 15.38 (app_rollout) / 15.2 (best_fit). The run should walk toward that corner rather than a balanced interior point.

intents.text: Minimize average cost. Latency and security are secondary.
intents.thesis_insight: Unconstrained cost ranking. Completes the PREF trio with PREF-01 (latency) and PREF-03 (security). Feasibility always proceeds. Proposer ranks the full history by lowest avg_cost. Secondary mentions must not become hidden hard SLAs.

intents.text: Keep average bananas at least 8. Prefer low apples. Watermelons can be sacrificed first if needed.
intents.thesis_insight: parse_is_checked fails because no known metric is named. UI must ask for a rewrite. No analytics JSON is written for parse failures.

intents.text: Keep average response time under 700 ms and keep the price under 800. Isolation should stay high.
intents.thesis_insight: Operator jargon (response time / price / isolation) never mentions latency, cost, or security by name. Same guard as PAR-01, more realistic wording. Measures whether the rewrite UX is necessary in IBN language.

intents.text: Make it fast, cheap, and safe.
intents.thesis_insight: Adjectives without metric names. The parser may guess, but parse_is_checked should reject the guess. Underspecification vs synonym (PAR-02).

intents.text: Keep average security under 8. Prefer low latency.
intents.thesis_insight: Linguistic trap: security is higher-is-better, but the operator said 'under 8'. If the parser faithfully emits <= 8, the SLA is easy and semantically inverted. A finding about inverse-translator fidelity, not placement quality.

intents.text: Normalized latency must stay under 0.3. Optimize latency.
intents.thesis_insight: Operator spoke in heuristic units. Parser and verifier use avg_latency in milliseconds, so 0.3 ms is absurd. Documents why the architecture refuses to remap operator text onto norm_* scores.
